solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient city captured in erudite books

indicators.note: the ancient city is held captive inside the word for erudite

parts.note: erudite means well-read, literate
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city of the Bible

explanation.surface: An old city's capture is recounted in learned volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is the body of written works, so books collectively stand for it.

clue.text: Girl is to receive Religious Instruction

indicators.note: the word is takes in the abbreviation, receiving it inside

parts.note: taken as written
RI is the school abbreviation for Religious Instruction

explanation.surface: A girl is due to have scripture lessons at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a girl's given name, so a girl is an example.

clue.text: Issue Oriental blend

parts.note: Oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
to blend is to merge

explanation.surface: A new release of an Eastern tea blend.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out, a synonym of the verb in the grid.

clue.text: Stagger to us and collapse

indicators.note: collapse tells us the words to us and fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: We stagger and collapse in a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze or astonish them, a synonym.

clue.text: Initially thought to come from outer space

definitions.text: Initially thought to come from outer space

parts.words: Initially thought to come from outer space
parts.note: flying saucers and the like are believed by some to be alien craft, and they are known by a set of initials

explanation.surface: Something first believed to have arrived from beyond the Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' hints that the answer is an abbreviation made of initial letters: unidentified flying objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are popularly assumed to be alien spacecraft, sighted objects of unknown origin.

clue.text: Excuses may mean the taxman ignores some charges

definitions.meaning: to excuse someone is to let them off a duty

definitions.text: may mean the taxman ignores some charges
definitions.meaning: goods or people that are free of tax are said to be released from it

explanation.definitionFit: To exempt is to free from an obligation, matching both letting off and tax relief.

clue.text: Prepare to fight for a rump steak that's rare

indicators.note: rare suggests the steak is underdone, but here it signals the letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a bout by eating an underdone steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' looks like a cooking instruction for the steak, but it is the anagram signal on A RUMP STEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up arms is an idiom for getting ready to go to war or fight.

clue.text: Migrant workers in transit, moving round the East

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the abbreviation
moving says the letters of in transit are shifted into a fresh order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Travelling labourers on the move around the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges IN TRANSIT to ITINRANTS, and 'round' puts that around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerants travel from place to place, often for work, so migrant workers are examples.

clue.text: Lent, for example, at an exorbitant rate

definitions.meaning: Lent is a period of abstaining from food or luxuries
describes something going quickly, at great speed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a period of abstinence and quickly, at speed.

clue.text: Cook sent in more soup

indicators.note: cook in the sense of doctoring or fiddling tells us these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: send more into the soup pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: New style navy

parts.note: a style or fashion is a mode
RN is short for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A fresh look for the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date or recent, a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Salerno a French city? Could be!

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of the Italian town might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an Italian seaport is really in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Salerno is an Italian port; its letters rearrange into the city on the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a city in north-central France, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Dismissed from brotherhood for not working

definitions.meaning: a monk or friar expelled from his religious fraternity
describes a machine that is broken

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both expelled from a religious order and broken down.

clue.text: Kissagram agency — an insincere profession?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a business supplying kisses with the mouth
a profession here means a declaration of belief made without meaning it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is idiom for support expressed but not acted upon, and read literally a kissing service.

clue.text: A sedentary occupation

parts.note: reads like a desk job, but means protesters occupying a place by remaining seated

explanation.surface: A job done sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest in which people occupy premises by sitting there is literally a seated occupation.

clue.text: Put a foot wrong and he may bail you out

definitions.text: Put a foot wrong and he may bail you out

parts.words: Put a foot wrong and he may bail you out
parts.note: in cricket, a batsman who steps out of the crease can be dismissed by the wicketkeeper knocking the bails off

explanation.surface: A friend who rescues you from trouble if you make a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bail you out' sounds like a rescue but means removing the bails. In cricket the bails sit on the stumps; the wicketkeeper can put the batsman out if their foot is outside the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumper is a colloquial name for a cricket wicketkeeper, who stumps batsmen.

clue.text: Go quietly, as a thief will do?

definitions.meaning: what a thief does is take things

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to creep stealthily and to rob.

clue.text: Reductions in fare for conferences

definitions.meaning: fare here means food, so cutting down what one eats
formal assemblies, such as the Japanese parliament or historical German councils

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both slimming regimes and legislative assemblies.

clue.text: Record finish of race

definitions.meaning: the line stretched across the finish that the winner breaks

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a recording medium and the finishing line of a race.

clue.text: Might be in or even out

indicators.note: out suggests the words in or are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something that could be inside or perhaps outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal and 'even' alone is the definition; 'Might be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth fabric flat with a hot appliance is to make it even.

clue.text: It is essential to return at six-fifty at the outside

indicators.note: at the outside says the Roman numerals sit around the other piece

parts.note: in Roman numerals six is VI and fifty is L

indicators.note: to return says the word at is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being back at ten to seven at the latest is crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the first 'at', and 'at the outside' wraps the Roman numerals for six and fifty around it. 'It is' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means absolutely necessary, a synonym of essential.

clue.text: It makes people unfit for high positions

definitions.text: It makes people unfit for high positions

parts.words: It makes people unfit for high positions
parts.note: reads like a disqualification for senior jobs, but means dizziness when up high

explanation.surface: A flaw that bars candidates from top jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is giddiness felt at heights, which stops sufferers standing in lofty places.

clue.text: The German rock singer teaching the French one

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or teaching
le is French for the
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A German rock vocalist instructing a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock singer' suggests a pop star; she is the siren of German legend who sat on a rock in the Rhine luring boatmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the legendary maiden on a Rhine rock whose song wrecked sailors.

clue.text: They're at liberty to be privileged citizens

definitions.meaning: people who are not enslaved or imprisoned
those granted the freedom of a city or borough

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both people not in bondage and holders of a city's honorary freedom.

clue.text: Cut loss from one of the Plagues of Egypt

definitions.text: one of the Plagues of Egypt
definitions.note: the plague of insects was one of the ten, so the plural swarm names it

indicators.note: from suggests the answer is made out of the letters of cut loss

explanation.surface: A trader wants to cut losses caused by a biblical disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm of grasshopper-like insects formed the eighth plague in Exodus.

clue.text: Head off from English county to see Italian region

indicators.note: head off says the first letter is removed from the county

parts.note: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District

explanation.surface: Travelling from northern England to see a part of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a landlocked region of central Italy, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Rising disgust

definitions.meaning: a rising is an uprising or rebellion
to disgust is to repel or sicken

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rebellion and to sicken or repel.

clue.text: A case for a seamstress

parts.note: reads like a job for a dressmaker, but means a small container for needles

explanation.surface: A job a dressmaker might take on.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and sewing items.

clue.text: Hothead raised the stake

indicators.note: in a down clue raised says the word is written upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: Etna is the Sicilian volcano, a hot head of a mountain

explanation.surface: An angry gambler upped the bet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a poker player's stake put in before the deal.

clue.text: Ten on trial perhaps — for being racialist?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters given could form another word

explanation.surface: Ten people in the dock for racist conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A racialist does not tolerate other races, making intolerant a fitting adjective.

clue.text: Produce a work of art from scratch

definitions.text: Produce a work of art from scratch

parts.words: Produce a work of art from scratch
parts.note: from scratch seems to mean from nothing, but means by scratching a plate

explanation.surface: Creating an artwork starting from nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching makes images by scratching lines into a coated plate, so art comes literally from scratches.

clue.text: Rose and made a speech without a single drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the speech word goes around the rest

parts.note: to make a speech is to orate, past tense orated
a single is one, the Roman numeral I
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone stood up and spoke without even a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of outside, so the speech word encloses the single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to originate or spring up, as a river rises at its source.
